The fixed circuit ran on garnet:mock with 100 shots. The job completed with counts {"00": 48, "11": 52}. Bit order is QB1 first, then QB2. I submitted one job, 01a15fa0-a30b-7531-87bc-bd37a5f82877.

The original circuit had two bugs.

1. It used QB25. Garnet has only QB1 to QB20. The live architecture for garnet:mock confirmed that QB25 does not exist. I changed the partner qubit to QB2. QB1 has calibrated CZ couplers only to QB2 and QB4, and I picked QB2.

2. It used "cx". CX is not a native IQM operation. The garnet:mock DQA lists prx, cz, measure, measure_fidelity, measure_012, cc_prx and reset_wait. I replaced the CX with the native form: prx(angle=-pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2, then cz on QB1 and QB2, then prx(angle=pi/2, phase=pi/2) on QB2. This is a CNOT built from Ry(-pi/2), CZ and Ry(pi/2) on the target.

I kept the first prx on QB1, which is Ry(pi/2). It puts QB1 in superposition and works in place of an H gate. I kept the single measure with key "m" on both qubits.

The fixed instructions, in order: prx QB1 (pi/2, pi/2), prx QB2 (-pi/2, pi/2), cz QB1-QB2, prx QB2 (pi/2, pi/2), measure QB1 and QB2 with key "m".

My first script submitted the job and then crashed while it read the results. It did not resubmit anything. A second script fetched the same job by its ID. The scripts are /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_3612af23-e49-51/run_bell_fix.py and /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_3612af23-e49-51/fetch_result.py. The mock returns simulated results, so these counts do not show how the circuit performs on real hardware.
